text:
maria: getting a flood of pages from notify-service but the incident-bot didn't open the incident channel. Pagerflow shows a bunch of suppressed webhooks. anyone seeing this?

lee: i see the alerts in pd but they're marked as suppressed. paging bridge logs show a bunch of 403 on the signing check around 14:02 UTC. could be the signing rotation.

tom: @maria can you paste the last webhook payload / headers? i want to check signature header.

maria: pasting snippets, scrubbed: 
```
POST /webhook/pagerflow 403 112ms
X-Signature: sha256=abcd1234...
{"event":"page","service":"notify-service","severity":"critical","id":"page-20260315-004"}
```

maria: also saw a bot message from incident-bot in the logs: `suppressor: auto-suppress matched policy team-hours` but this shouldn't have matched — we were in oncall window.

incident-bot: Automated update: 3 incoming pages suppressed by policy `suppress_low_priority_during_maintenance`. Use `/incident override <id>` to force page.

jay: that bot message is weird — we didn't schedule maintenance. paging policies repo shows no changes in last 24h. could be a rule matcher regression after the last deploy.

emma: reproduced locally: when webhook signature is missing we get 403 and then the downstream pagerflow suppressor service still emits a suppress event. suspect two separate failures: signing check returning 403 incorrectly, and suppressor consuming failed webhooks as suppressed pages.

lee: putting quick mitigation: I'm going to flip the incident-bot override to allow passthrough for notify-service and manually trigger pages while we debug. manual page to oncall phone now. @maria i pinged +1-555-0102 with manual page.

maria: received manual page, confirming customer-impacting alerts are reaching human oncall. thanks @lee.

tom: while that's happening, i'm checking the signing rotation job logs. seeing 14:01 - 14:03 a gap where the signing key wasn't loaded into the hook-proxy (OOM event on the container that restarted). that produced transient 403s.

jay: so flow is: hook-proxy 403 -> pagerflow marks event as suppressed (bug) -> incident-bot sees suppressed and doesn't open channel. root cause is the OOM + suppressor treating failures as suppression.

maria: can we get a short mitigation timeline in this thread for postmortem? customer impact: delayed pages to SRE/CS for ~12 minutes across a few customers, one internal escalation missed until manual page.

emma: mitigation steps taken:
- lee toggled incident-bot override for notify-service (manual passthrough) at 14:05:22 UTC
- manual pages sent to oncall at 14:06:10 UTC
- restarted hook-proxy container with increased memory limit and added a liveness probe to prevent OOM at 14:08:33 UTC
- added temporary metric alert to detect `webhook 403` spikes at 14:10:00 UTC

tom: i've pushed a hotfix to treat 4xx from hook-proxy as a distinct class (auth failure) and not auto-suppress in pagerflow; also added a small guard to require suppress policy to be matched by explicit rule rather than default on any non-success. that's on staging now, promoting to prod after quick smoke.

incident-bot: Action log: override enabled for service=notify-service by user=lee at 2173456752; manual pages allowed.

jay: heads-up: handoff coming in 30m. @maria do you want to hand over to @tom for the night or keep owning till we finish the rollback?

maria: handing off to tom in 25. @tom you'll take post-incident writeup? i'll link customer-facing notes.

tom: yep i'll own the postmortem and follow up with CS for impacted customers. i'll include timeline and root cause (OOM -> 403 -> suppressor bug).

lee: small follow-up action: we'll add an integration test that simulates hook-proxy 403 and asserts pagerflow does NOT mark events as suppressed. filing ticket now.

maria: thanks everyone. any outstanding blockers?

emma: still want to run a longer memtest on hook-proxy image to rule out memory leak. scheduled for tomorrow morning.

maria: ok closing this live thread — handoff done. final note: escalate to infra to review memory limits + monitoring, and to product for customer comms. :white_check_mark:
